importance_ranking.reason: High visual variation across sub-types — single cabin vs multi-seat block, Indian squat vs Western commode, mobile vs fixed, combined toilet+bathroom vs toilet-only. Buyers use the image to confirm product type before reading any text; wrong type is an immediate skip.

No. of Seats, Toilet Seat type, Wall Material, and Module Type are non-interchangeable shortlisting criteria — especially for government tender procurement where specs are mandated. Listings without these specs cannot be evaluated or compared.

Highly fragmented market with hundreds of regional manufacturers. Construction contractors and government buyers compare per-piece rates aggressively within their known spec tier. India price sensitivity is high and price is a primary decision lever once type and spec are confirmed.

importance_ranking.brand_important_reason: Market is highly fragmented across regional FRP fabricators; Sintex is a recognised name but buyers do not search by brand — they search by spec, seat count, and price.
importance_ranking.reason: Institutional buyers (PWD, municipal corporations) evaluate manufacturer supply capacity, past government supply track record, and installation credentials during vendor selection — important but secondary to spec and price confirmation.

importance_ranking.unit_note: Multi-seat blocks may be quoted per block or per seat, and rental deployments quote per piece per day/month — but B2B sale listings universally quote per piece and no buyer questions this.
importance_ranking.reason: Unit is entirely implied for a discrete prefabricated cabin unit. No buyer ever questions whether an FRP modular toilet is sold per piece.

top_configurator_specs.reason: Defines the scale of the unit from single cabin to 10-seat block — non-interchangeable across procurement requirements and the largest price delta of any spec in this category.

Indian squat pan vs Western commode vs Urinal Only are non-interchangeable functional configurations that serve different user populations and tender specifications, with meaningful price and fitment differences.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Agent 3 market research explicitly identifies wall thickness as the primary quality differentiator in this category, ranging from 2mm economy to 8–30mm premium sandwich panel — buyers cannot compare durability or quality without this dimension, which is not captured by Wall Material alone.

Sellers need to know whether the buyer requires a bio-digester unit, septic tank connection, or chemical system to confirm infrastructure compatibility and supply the correct product variant — these are non-interchangeable and represent distinct product sub-types.

Site space constraints make footprint dimensions a real buyer requirement — Agent 3 identifies standard sizes clustering at 3×3 ft, 4×4 ft, and 4×6 ft, and sellers need this to confirm the unit fits the allocated space and to price correctly.
